pages/projects/project_11.html.text: Project Details Java Compiler for a Subset of an Advanced Language Description This project focuses on illustrating essential aspects of software engineering through the development of a complex application: a Java-based compiler for a subset of an advanced programming language. Key aspects include compliance with requirements, software design, validation and verification techniques, and a structured quality process. The project aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of programming language concepts while adhering to rigorous software engineering principles. Context: Project for the course "Projet génie logiciel" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 3 months Team Size: 6 people Timeline: Nov 2023 - Jan 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: Java, Assembly Tools: Git, Maven, Javadoc Concepts: Software Engineering, Code Generation, UML Modeling Tasks Studied requirements focusing on language definition, semantics, and target machine. Designed a modular, scalable compiler architecture using UML. Applied validation and verification to ensure compliance with project requirements. Used Git with branching, pull requests, and code reviews for version control. Documented code with Javadoc, adding tags for organized, accessible API details. Used Maven for dependency management and automated builds via `pom.xml`. Gained deeper insights into compiler theory and programming language concepts.

pages/projects/project_16.html.text: Project Details Aerodesign Competition Team Description Carancho Aerodesign, founded in 2004, is a project at the Federal University of Santa Maria (UFSM) that brings together students from various engineering disciplines to design and construct radio-controlled aircraft. The team participates annually in the SAE Brasil Aerodesign competition, where students showcase their skills in aeronautical engineering. The project aims to develop innovative solutions in aircraft construction, focusing on structural efficiency and aerodynamics. Context: Aerodesign Competition Team. Local: Santa Maria, Brazil Duration: 2 years Team Size: 30 person Timeline: May 2020 - Apr 2022 Technologies Used Programming Language: Python, Matlab, C Tools: SolidWorks, Abaqus, Ansys, Excel, XFLR5 Techniques: Loads analysis, aeroelasticity, structural integrity testing Tasks Led a structural block comprising three departments: Structures Analysis, Loads and Aeroelasticity, and CAD, managing task assignments and progress tracking. Achieved 10th place in the national SAE Aerodesign competition in 2021, demonstrating expertise in analyzing structural integrity and aeroelastic behavior of aircraft. Conducted wing load analysis for structural integrity under various flight conditions. Performed load analysis on vertical tail and control surfaces to ensure stability. Analyzed landing gear loads for multiple landing scenarios and braking conditions. Executed engine mount load analysis, evaluating vertical and lateral forces.

pages/projects/project_17.html.text: Project Details Description This project aims to support aerospace engineering students through teaching and outreach activities, helping them develop skills beyond the classroom while increasing community engagement with academic events. EP Aero is Brazil's first pilot school for Aerospace Engineering. Context: Educational outreach project. Local: Santa Maria, Brazil Duration: 1 year and 3 months Team Size: 15 person Timeline: Nov 2022 - Jan 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: JavaScript, HTML, CSS Tools: SonarQube, Scalingo, Node, React, Git, CI/CD Tasks Responsible for structuring internal projects, contributing to the selection process of new members, allocating members to activities, delegating and tracking tasks, and initiating partnerships with aerospace professionals, institutions, and projects. Involved in planning aerospace mini-courses for students and the external community, reaching over 200 participants. Developed an interactive website to manage aerospace events and workshops, utilizing JavaScript frameworks to enhance event registration and the presentation of activities. Integrated SonarQube in the CI/CD pipeline to ensure continuous code quality analysis, detect bugs, and enhance security.

pages/projects/project_6.html.text: Project Details Real-Time Control System of a Magnetic Suspension Description This project involves designing a real-time control system for a magnetic suspension system. The approach includes system modeling using physical equations and linearizing around the equilibrium point, followed by discretization and stability analysis. MATLAB simulations validate the model, and control is implemented with a state feedback LQR regulator and a state observer based on a Kalman filter, using Simulink for real-time simulation. Context: Project for the course "Contrôle-commande temps réel des systèmes cyber-physiques" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 1 month Team Size: Individual Timeline: Oct 2024 - Nov 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: MATLAB Tools: Simulink Concepts: System Modeling, LQR, Kalman Filter, Real-Time Control Tasks Modeling the magnetic suspension system using physical equations and linearizing around the equilibrium point. Performing model discretization and stability analysis, validated through MATLAB simulations. Implementing state feedback control with an LQR regulator and a state observer using a Kalman filter in Simulink. Simulating the control system in real-time to ensure precise system response and stability.

pages/projects/project_3.html.text: Project Details Description Image Filter Development on System on Chip This project involves developing an image filter on a System on Chip (SoC) platform using C++ and SystemC. The project includes implementing a communication bus for efficient data transfer between SoC modules and programming a finite state machine (FSM) in Verilog to manage pixel-level filtering processes. Additionally, a custom testbench is created to generate test images and analyze waveform outputs for performance evaluation. Context: Project for the course "Modélisation transactionnelle des systèmes sur puces" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 4 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Sep 2024 - Dec 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: C++, SystemC, Verilog Tools: SystemC, MakeFile Concepts: FSM Design, Data Bus Communication Tasks Implementing an image filter in C++ and SystemC with a communication bus for data transfer between SoC modules. Programming a finite state machine (FSM) in Verilog to control pixel-level filtering. Developing a testbench in C++ to generate signals and analyze waveforms for filter validation. Documenting design and validation processes to support future enhancements and optimizations.

pages/projects/project_5.html.text: Project Details Fault Injection in Memory Description This project focuses on fault injection in memory systems to evaluate fault tolerance and protect against side-channel attacks. The project involves injecting Single Event Upset (SEU) faults, setting up a Design Under Test (DUT) with a testbench for fault simulation, and automating the process using ModelSim and TCL scripts. Results are analyzed to identify critical vulnerabilities, and strategies are proposed to enhance fault tolerance. Context: Project for the course "Sécurité et sûreté matérielle" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 2 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Oct 2024 - Nov 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: TCL Tools: ModelSim Concepts: Fault Injection, Fault Tolerance, Attack Prevention Tasks Injecting SEU faults to evaluate fault tolerance and prevent potential attacks. Setting up a Design Under Test (DUT) and creating a testbench to simulate faults. Automating simulations with ModelSim and TCL scripts to streamline fault injection. Analyzing results to identify critical components and vulnerabilities, and proposing fault-tolerance techniques.

pages/projects/project_12.html.text: Project Details Spell Checker Description This project involves developing a Spell Checker with efficient data structures and algorithms for optimized word search and correction. Key components include implementing tries, hash tables, and balanced binary trees, and comparing the performance of various search and sorting algorithms to determine the most efficient approach for spell-checking. Context: Project for the course "Algorithmique et programmation" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 4 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Oct 2023 - Jan 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: C Tools: Git, MakeFile, Valgrind Concepts: Sequential Search, Sorting Algorithms, Tries, Hash Tables, Balanced Binary Trees Tasks Implementation of advanced data structures, including tries, hash tables, and balanced binary trees. Compared efficiency of search and sorting algorithms for spell-checking tasks. Organized project structure using Makefiles for seamless compilation and execution. Performance and complexity analysis to optimize processing speed and memory usage.

pages/projects/project_9.html.text: Project Details Embedded Software for a CubeSat Description This project involves developing embedded software for a CubeSat, focusing on the implementation of communication protocols for real-time data exchange between the satellite’s microcontroller and the ground station. The project also includes the development of autonomous embedded software for efficient task management, incorporating attitude control algorithms to maintain optimal satellite orientation during operation. Context: Project for the course "FabLab" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 5 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Sep 2023 - Jan 2024 Technologies Used Development Boards: ESP32, ESP8266 Programming Languages: C Tools: Arduino IDE Concepts: UDP, Real-Time Control, FSM Design Tasks Implemented communication protocols for real-time data exchange between the CubeSat’s microcontroller and the ground station. Developed autonomous embedded software for effective task management in satellite operations. Incorporated attitude control algorithms to ensure optimal orientation and stability of the CubeSat. Tested and validated communication and control systems to ensure reliability during missions.

pages/projects/project_2.html.text: Project Details Description CVA6 Processor Upgrade This project focuses on the validation and evaluation of the CVA6 processor upgraded to a 128-bit RISC-V architecture. The aim is to ensure robust performance of the new processor design while automating the validation process to enhance efficiency. This entails a detailed analysis of microarchitecture through reverse engineering and meticulous documentation review. The project also involves developing and automating tests in Assembly and C to validate functionality and optimize FPGA performance. Context: Project for the course "Projet de Systèmes Embarqués" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 5 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Sep 2024 - Jan 2025 Technologies Used Development Boards: FPGA Programming Languages: C, Assembly, Verilog Tools: GCC, GDB, Vivado, Verilator Concepts: Microarchitecture Analysis, Validation, Low-Level Software Tasks Currently upgrading the CVA6 processor to 128-bit architecture, aimed at enhancing performance capabilities. Developing an automated testing framework for efficient validation processes. In-depth microarchitecture analysis in progress to identify key optimizations for FPGA synthesis and improve area and performance. Creating comprehensive documentation to support future enhancements and maintenance.

pages/projects/project_18.html.text: Project Details Webservatório - Online Astronomical Observations Description This project focuses on promoting astronomy and space engineering through engaging online astronomical observations and discussions on YouTube livestreams. Webservatório brings students together with experts, helping to increase public interest in astronomy and aerospace topics. Context: Educational outreach project. Local: Santa Maria, Brazil Duration: 1 year Team Size: 6 members Timeline: May 2021 - Apr 2022 Tasks Served as the student coordinator, managing project activities and connecting with professionals for events. Built partnerships with other projects to enhance outreach and engagement. Hosted YouTube broadcasts, reaching over 40,000 viewers to promote interest in aerospace topics. Represented the project on the "+Conexões" program linked to the Brazil Conference at Harvard & MIT.

pages/projects/project_10.html.text: Project Details 2-PAM Digital Transmission Chain Simulation Description This project involves simulating a 2-PAM (Pulse Amplitude Modulation) digital transmission chain using MATLAB. It focuses on modeling and implementing both analog and digital filters for effective signal processing. Additionally, the project includes estimating the Power Spectral Density (PSD) using FFT and IFFT techniques to measure and analyze the spectral response of the filters, ensuring optimal performance in the transmission chain. Context: Project for the course "Communication numérique" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 5 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Jan 2024 - May 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: MATLAB Concepts: Signal Processing, Analog and Digital Filter Tasks Modeled and implemented analog and digital filters in MATLAB for effective signal processing. Estimated the Power Spectral Density (PSD) using FFT and IFFT to analyze the spectral response of the filters. Simulated the 2-PAM digital transmission chain to evaluate performance metrics and optimize filter design. Analyzed simulation results to ensure reliability and effectiveness of the transmission system.

pages/projects/project_8.html.text: Project Details Radio Systems for IoT Devices Description This project focuses on developing and analyzing radio systems for IoT devices, with an emphasis on filter modeling for Software-Defined Radio (SDR) applications. It includes digital signal simulations in both time and frequency domains, integrating Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) techniques. The transmission chain is modeled and simulated to evaluate interference sources and explore performance trade-offs in IoT radio systems. Context: Project for the course "Systèmes radio pour les objets connectés" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 5 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Sep 2023 - Jan 2024 Technologies Used Concepts: Software-Defined Radio (SDR), Digital and Analog Filter Modeling, OFDM, Transmission Chain Analysis Tasks Modeled digital and analog filters applicable. Simulated digital signals in time and frequency domains, incorporating OFDM concepts. Developed and simulated a transmission chain to assess interference sources and performance trade-offs. Analyzed simulation results to optimize filter design and improve IoT communication reliability.

pages/projects/project_1.html.text: Project Details Development of a Low-Level OS Kernel Description Developed a low-level OS kernel with core functionalities in communication, interrupt management, and process handling using QEMU for emulation. Context: Project for the course "Projet de Conception de Systèmes d'Exploitation" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 5 months Team Size: Individual project Timeline: Sep 2023 - Jan 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: C, Assembly Protocols: UART Tools: QEMU, GCC, GDB, Valgrind Concepts: RISC-V, Processor Architecture, Real-Time Systems, Operating System Kernel Design, Interrupt Handling, Process Management Results and Conclusions Achieved a grade of 17 out of 20. Implemented a low-level OS kernel with successful UART communication for data exchange. Developed an effective interrupt management system with preemptive scheduling. Enabled dynamic process creation for improved memory management. Code was well-structured, documented, and exceeded minimal project requirements. Identified opportunities for future enhancements, including keyboard handling and graphical interface improvements.

pages/projects/project_4.html.text: Project Details FIR Filter Description This project focused on designing and implementing a Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter for signal processing applications using VHDL. The design was verified with a custom testbench in ModelSim and synthesized using Synopsys Design Vision. Placement and routing were conducted on an FPGA, with final performance validation using an oscilloscope to ensure signal fidelity and timing accuracy. Context: Project for the course "Projet de conception d'électronique numérique" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 5 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Jan 2024 - May 2024 Technologies Used Development Boards: FPGA (Spartan-3) Programming Languages: VHDL Tools: ModelSim, Synopsys Design Vision, SpyGlass, Xilinx Concepts: Filter Design, Placement and Routing, Signal Processing, Testbench Verification Tasks Designed a FIR filter in VHDL to process digital signals with high accuracy. Verified filter functionality using a ModelSim testbench. Synthesized the design in Synopsys Design Vision and optimized FPGA placement and routing. Performed real-time signal testing on an oscilloscope to validate performance.

pages/projects/project_13.html.text: Project Details Firstep Mobile Application Description This project focuses on developing the "Firstep" mobile application, designed to help users share experiences and start new activities. The application is built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frameworks, and is deployed on the Scalingo cloud platform with PostgreSQL for user management. Security and code quality are monitored through SonarQube. Context: Project for the course "Création d'Entreprise" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 5 months Team Size: 6 person Timeline: Jan 2024 - May 2024 Technologies Used Programming Languages: HTML, CSS, JavaScript Tools: PostgreSQL, Scalingo, SonarQube, React, Node, Git, CI/CD Tasks Developed a user-friendly interface using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frameworks. Managed user data and authentication with PostgreSQL on the Scalingo cloud. Ensured code quality and security standards through SonarQube integration.

pages/projects/project_7.html.text: Project Details Real-Time Control System for Autonomous Vehicle Description This project involves developing a real-time control system for an autonomous vehicle, focusing on implementing precise control loops and dynamic equations for accurate navigation. The project integrates motor and steering control with FreeRTOS for real-time task management and leverages the NXP FRDM-KL25Z microcontroller programmed with MCU Expresso. Context: Project for the course "Contrôle-commande temps réel des systèmes cyber-physiques" in the Embedded Systems and Connected Objects master's program. Local: Institut Polytechnique de Grenoble (INP Grenoble), Grenoble, France Duration: 5 months Team Size: 2 people Timeline: Sep 2024 - Jan 2025 Technologies Used Development Boards: NXP FRDM-KL25Z Programming Languages: C Tools: FreeRTOS, MCU Expresso Concepts: Real-Time Control, System Modeling Tasks Developing control loops and dynamic equations for real-time precision in autonomous vehicle navigation. Integrating motor and steering control with FreeRTOS for effective real-time task scheduling. Programming the NXP FRDM-KL25Z microcontroller using MCU Expresso for control system implementation. Testing and validating the system to ensure responsiveness and accuracy in navigation tasks.

pages/projects/project_14.html.text: Project Details Interactive Study Guides Description This project involves creating interactive study guides for solid mechanics using Python and Jupyter Notebook. The guides simplify complex topics through the use of interactive graphics, enhancing the learning experience for students. Context: Personal project. Local: Remote/Independent Duration: 2 months Team Size: Individual Timeline: May 2021 - Jul 2021 Technologies Used Programming Language: Python Tools: Jupyter Notebook, Matplotlib, NumPy Tasks Developed interactive study guides to explain complex solid mechanics concepts. Utilized Jupyter Notebook to create engaging learning materials with graphics. Prepared comprehensive project report. (Report)

pages/projects/project_15.html.text: Project Details Low-Cost Educational Mini-Rocket Kit Description This project involved designing and assembling a low-cost educational mini-rocket kit aimed at promoting interest in space among students. The kit is used in public schools to provide hands-on learning experiences related to aerospace engineering and rocketry. Context: Educational outreach project. Local: Santa Maria, Brazil Duration: 4 months Team Size: 3 person Timeline: Mar 2020 - Jul 2020 Technologies Used Tools: Latex Concepts: Outreach Project Tasks Designed and assembled a mini-rocket kit for educational purposes. Presented the kit in public schools to promote hands-on learning experiences. Conducted initial research and secured resources for project implementation.

pages/experience/experience_2.html.text: Project Details Flight Control Researcher Description This research project focused on developing advanced flight control algorithms to enhance satellite tracking accuracy in formation flight. The objective was to model dynamic equations and design control systems that would optimize trajectory control while minimizing measurement noise. Context: Research project during the third year of Aerospace Engineering studies. Company: Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica (ITA) Local: São José dos Campos, Brazil (remote) Duration: 1 year Team Size: Individual research Timeline: Sep 2022 - Aug 2023 Technologies Used Programming Languages: MATLAB Tools: Simulink Concepts: Flight Dynamics, Control Systems, Kalman Filtering Results and Conclusions Developed Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithms in MATLAB to improve satellite tracking accuracy for formation flight, reducing measurement noise by 81.7%. Modeled linear and non-linear dynamic equations for satellite flight dynamics using MATLAB to simulate formation flight scenarios. Designed Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and servomechanism with state feedback controllers in MATLAB for satellite trajectory control. Implemented control systems in Simulink to optimize attitude control and avoid actuator saturation.

pages/experience/experience_3.html.text: Project Details Machine Learning Intern Description This internship focused on developing a virtual clothing fitting tool for an e-commerce company, utilizing machine learning algorithms for image segmentation through convolutional neural networks. I was responsible for the backend development, optimizing workflow performance and enhancing model accuracy using various frameworks and techniques. Context: Non-mandatory internship during the third year of Aerospace Engineering studies. Company: Dafiti Group Local: São Paulo, Brazil (remote) Duration: 8 months Team Size: 5 people Timeline: Feb 2022 - Sep 2022 Technologies Used Programming Languages: Python Tools: Git, U-Net, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn, OpenCV Concepts: Image Segmentation, Machine Learning, Neural Networks Results and Conclusions Developed Python algorithms for image segmentation using U-Net convolutional neural networks. Migrated machine learning workflows to GPU, reducing training times by 71%. Explored performance optimizations with PyTorch and TensorFlow frameworks. Created and managed training, validation, and test datasets for model development. Managed project versions with Git, tracked model improvements, and collaborated across different branches.

pages/experience/experience_1.html.text: Project Details Description Satellite Firmware Development Intern This internship involved developing embedded software for data communication between a nanosatellite payload board and its central computer. The project aimed to ensure robust performance for upcoming radiation tests, focusing on real-time communication and automated testing processes. Context: Mandatory internship for a master's degree in Embedded Systems and Connected Objects. Company: TIMA Laboratory Local: Grenoble, Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, France Duration: 3 months Team Size: 3 members Timeline: May 2024 - Aug 2024 Technologies Used Development Boards: STM32 microcontrollers, ESP32 Programming Languages: C, Bash Protocols: I2C, UART Tools: GDB, GCC, OpenOCD, CMake, SVN Concepts: Radiation Testing, Real-Time Communication Results and Conclusions Developed embedded software for data communication between a nanosatellite payload board and its central computer, ensuring robust performance for upcoming radiation tests. Designed and optimized real-time communication protocols (I2C, UART) in C for STM32 microcontrollers, achieving a 99.85% reduction in execution time. Automated testing processes with a custom Bash script interface for algorithm selection and error tracking. Managed project versions with SVN and integrated automated builds using CMake. Used GDB for debugging and OpenOCD for programming embedded systems.
